title: seccomp: restrict socketpair to AF_UNIX and AF_TIPC
body:
The default profile blocks socket(2) for AF_VSOCK, but allows socketpair(2) unconditionally. A container can therefore call socketpair() with a family that socket() would not permit, and the kernel will still try to load that family's module.

Only AF_UNIX and AF_TIPC implement socketpair, so every other family fails anyway. Drop socketpair from the unconditional allow list and allow it only when argument 0 is AF_UNIX or AF_TIPC.

These are allow rules, so a value with the upper 32 bits set does not match, and no mask is needed as for the socket deny rules.

Calls with any other family now fail with ENOSYS, the profile default, instead of the kernel's error. On ABIs that use socketcall(2) the arguments cannot be filtered, so socketpair stays unrestricted there, as for socket.

Add a test for the allowed socketpair domains and regenerate seccomp.json.

Fixes #1316

comments.body: these modules can also be loaded through socket(2), no?  So how does this make any difference?

> these modules can also be loaded through socket(2), no? So how does this make any difference?

the current socket rule does seem to block AF_VSOCK, so I guess this avoids at least this one.

> these modules can also be loaded through socket(2), no? So how does this make any difference?

Yes.  That's why I think we should adopt Docker's approach here that restricts address families.
